title: Time Jump: 12:15, the Centrifuge Room Decision Is Signed

fields.scenarioTitle: Hairline Crack — Centrifuge Failure, Exposure Clocks & Rumor
fields.narration:
Read only the version that matches the decision the room recorded at I-12, then read the common section.

VERSION A (room held until the vendor inspects): It is now 12:15 on Tuesday, 13 October 2026. The Biology department head has your written decision on the Lindgren third-floor shared centrifuge room. The whole room stays closed until Prairieline Lab Services inspects on Friday, 16 October. Neither centrifuge has been touched. Dr. Tomas Eklund's tubes from the run that ended at 10:10 are still locked inside the second unit. Four groups have lost their afternoon slots. Dr. Tomas Eklund's postdoc is standing at the ground-floor front desk with an empty ice bucket, asking who signed the decision.

VERSION B (phased reopening, failed unit tagged out): It is now 12:15 on Tuesday, 13 October 2026. The Biology department head has your written decision on the Lindgren third-floor shared centrifuge room. The room will reopen in phases. The failed centrifuge stays tagged out under its sealed lid. Four groups want back in at the same time, and nobody has said who goes first. Dr. Tomas Eklund's postdoc is standing at the ground-floor front desk with an empty ice bucket, asking when she can go up.

READ IN BOTH VERSIONS: The campus forum thread 'LAB LEAK IN LINDGREN' has passed 400 upvotes. The Halvorsen Herald has moved its deadline to 14:00, but its editor says the web story will go up 'when it's ready.' The Dean's office still needs the text of its same-day note to Lindgren staff by 15:00. The second cell biology technician was referred back to the Occupational Health Clinic but has not arrived. The EHS portal clock board for LI-2026-0142 now shows a new sponsor row: Iowa Corn Growers Board, 72 hours, due 16 October at 09:02. Nobody has acted on it yet. The BSO's first written report to the IBC chair is still a draft.
worldState: Clock: 12:15, Tuesday, 13 October 2026. The stop-work began at 09:02, more than three hours ago.
The written decision on the Lindgren 3F shared centrifuge room has reached the Biology department head (Version A: closed until Friday; Version B: phased reopening, failed unit tagged out).
Prairieline Lab Services (PLS-SR-26-3318): the earliest rotor inspection is Friday 16 Oct, 08:00–12:00. The vendor has asked that neither centrifuge be run before then.
Dr. Tomas Eklund's postdoc is at the Lindgren ground-floor front desk with an empty ice bucket. Four third-floor groups want access.
HSU Campus Forum thread 'LAB LEAK IN LINDGREN' has passed 400 upvotes. The @lindgren_late_nights post is still circulating.
The Halvorsen Herald's deadline is 14:00. The editor may publish online before then.
The Dean's same-day note to Lindgren staff is due by 15:00. Its wording has not been agreed.
The second cell biology technician was referred back to the Occupational Health Clinic and has not been seen. The clinic's last walk-in slot is 16:15 and it closes at 17:00.

EHS portal clock board, LI-2026-0142: there is a new row for Iowa Corn Growers Board notice, 72 hours from discovery, due 16 Oct 2026 09:02, status OPEN, no owner assigned. The HSU 7-day row (due 20 Oct 09:02) is still showing.
The BSO's report to the IBC chair is still in draft. The board row 'BSO reports to IBC chair' is due 16 Oct 09:20 and is still OPEN. The IBC chair has not set a classification.
The ULT-L4-09 discrepancy has been explained as a transfer recorded only on paper. The 14 vials are in ULT-L4-12, and the EHS portal record has not yet been corrected.
fields.facilitatorNote: Read only the version that matches the I-12 decision. If the room never made a written decision, tell them so and have them make it now before you go on. Watch for these actions: the BSO brings the EHS portal status and the door sign into line with the decision. RC takes ownership of the 72-hour Iowa Corn Growers Board row and notifies the program contact, because the shorter term wins. The BSO finishes and sends the report to the IBC chair (Biosafety plan 6) and keeps chasing the technician's re-referral. In Version B, check that someone controls who enters first and that nobody touches the failed unit.

instructorNote: This card returns players to the decision they made at I-12 and makes them carry it out at the same moment as the sponsor clock, the IBC report and the technician's referral, while the media pressure keeps growing. Watch whether RC acts on the 72-hour row without being prompted and whether the BSO's draft becomes a sent report to the IBC chair.
